name: Measuring Trust and Knowledge
title: Measuring Trust and Knowledge
answer: Districts can measure whether professional learning about AI is actually working by using validated instruments for teachers' trust in AI tools and their knowledge of ethical AI use, called Intelligent TPACK. Measuring before and after training keeps professional learning honest, because a session that feels good but changes nothing is not working. Leaders should share the results with teachers and use them to improve support.

sections.body: This idea is about measuring two things that shape how well teachers take up AI: their trust in AI based tools and their knowledge of how to use AI ethically in teaching. Trust is not one feeling but several, covering perceived benefits, concerns about transparency, anxieties, and confidence. Knowledge is also layered, covering AI tools themselves, their use for feedback and monitoring, subject specific tools, and ethical judgment. Without measurement, leaders guess at where teachers stand and design support that may miss the real gaps. Measuring gives leaders a factual starting point for designing better support.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: A district can survey teachers with the trust instrument to see where they stand on benefits, transparency concerns, anxieties, and confidence, then shape support around the weak spots. The Intelligent TPACK instrument can be given before and after professional learning, and the change between the two shows whether teachers are growing. The text does not give separate grade band guidance, so the practice applies across a district's teaching staff rather than to particular year groups. Surveys alone are not enough, and the text pairs them with observations and the time study from Chapter 17 to give a fuller picture. Leaders then share the results with teachers and use them to improve the training.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text labels this idea with research support, citing validated instruments. Nazaretsky et al. (2022) developed and validated an instrument for measuring teachers' trust in AI based tools, covering perceived benefits, concerns about transparency, anxieties, and confidence. Çelik (2023) developed a validated instrument for teachers' knowledge of ethical AI use in teaching, called Intelligent TPACK, covering knowledge of AI tools, their use for feedback and monitoring, subject specific tools, and ethical judgment. The text states that using the knowledge instrument before and after professional learning shows whether teachers are growing, and that surveys, observations, and the time study from Chapter 17 together give a fuller picture.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The text sets limits on what measurement can do. A training that feels good but does not change knowledge or practice is not working, so results should not be treated as a formality or a public relations exercise. Surveys on their own give only part of the picture, which is why the text pairs them with observations and the time study from Chapter 17. Leaders are told to share results with teachers and use them to improve, which keeps the purpose developmental rather than judgmental. The decisions about what to do with the findings stay with people, and the text does not describe any automatic action that follows from the scores.
